# You can’t withdraw your money. Here’s what we know and what we’re doing.

*By Inês, Product Designer at Pinha · 10 November 2026*

Since Friday, 6 November, you have not been able to withdraw your money from Pinha. Deposits and round-ups have stopped too.

Our payments partner, Northvale Payments, blocked all outgoing transfers at 09:00 that morning, without warning us that it was about to do so.

**Your money has not been lost. It remains in a safeguarded account, separate from Northvale’s own money. Northvale cannot use it for its own purposes. But we cannot move it until Northvale releases it.**

That distinction matters. So does this: knowing your money is safeguarded does not pay your rent. It does not buy your medication or stop a deadline from passing. The money belongs to you, and right now you cannot access it.

You deserve an explanation of what happened, what we got wrong, and what you can do today.

## If you urgently need your money

**If you need your savings for rent, medical costs, or because you have lost your job, email urgent@pinha.example with the subject line URGENTE.** Tell us what makes your situation urgent and whether there is a deadline.

We are trying to get Northvale to release money individually for urgent cases. This is a request we are pushing them to act on, not a guaranteed route to a withdrawal. We cannot promise that they will approve a release or that it will happen before your deadline.

I wish I could write something more reassuring. I won’t tell you that sending an email will fix this when we don’t know that it will.

**We have also cancelled the monthly fee for November and December for everyone.** You do not need to ask us to do that. It does not make up for losing access to your savings, but you should not be paying us during this period.

## What happened

Northvale Payments is an electronic money institution based in Vilnius. It is the partner that holds Pinha customers’ money.

On **Wednesday, 4 November**, Northvale emailed us a notice of “commercial termination,” giving us 30 days’ notice. The explanation it gave was a “risk appetite review.” We have not been given a more specific reason.

On **Friday, 6 November, at 09:00**, Northvale blocked all outgoing transfers. It did not warn us before doing so. That block came two days into the 30-day notice period, contrary to what the notice said. Deposits and round-ups also stopped.

On **Saturday, 7 November**, we filed complaints with Banco de Portugal and the Lithuanian central bank.

Today, **Tuesday, 10 November**, withdrawals remain blocked.

I am angry that Northvale gave us a notice period and then cut off access to your money two days later. “Risk appetite review” explains nothing useful to someone trying to withdraw savings they need this week.

But our anger at Northvale does not remove our responsibility to you.

## What “safeguarded” means here

Your money is held in a safeguarded account, separate from Northvale’s own funds. It is not money Northvale can use to run its business.

That is why we are saying your money has not been lost.

Safeguarding and access are different things, though. The money remains there, but Northvale is blocking its movement. Pinha cannot bypass that block or transfer the balances ourselves.

I don’t want to hide that behind the word “safe.” Your balance being protected is important. Being able to use it when you need it is important too. Right now, we are failing to provide that access.

## We have signed a new partner. The move is not finished.

We have already signed with **Ostra Bank, based in Lisbon**, to become our new payments partner.

For the migration to go ahead, we need Northvale to provide the balances file and we need approval from Banco de Portugal. Signing with Ostra is a necessary step, but it does not, on its own, unblock your money.

Our current estimate for the migration is **10 to 15 working days**. It is an estimate, not a confirmed schedule or a promise that your money will be available within that period. The outstanding steps depend on Northvale and regulatory approval, and we cannot give you a reliable withdrawal date today.

Please do not treat that estimate as a date you can safely commit to a landlord, a seller or anyone else waiting for payment.

Rui, our CEO, is spending today in calls with lawyers and Banco de Portugal. We are working to get the balances released and complete the move. Until the required steps are confirmed, we will not turn our best estimate into a deadline we may miss.

## What we got wrong

We relied on one payments partner. We had no backup.

We were naive about what that dependency could mean for you if the relationship failed. That was our mistake. You did not choose Northvale; you chose Pinha. It was our job to think through what would happen if the partner holding your money stopped cooperating.

I work on the product. I designed the screen that says: “Your money is always yours, take it out anytime.”

I look at that sentence now and feel sick. We put those words in front of you, and you had every reason to rely on them.

One user from Porto wrote to us in capitals. She has been saving for three years for a car deposit, and the dealership has given her until this Friday, 13 November. I read her message on the metro and nearly cried.

She does not need my tears. She needs her money before Friday. I cannot tell her today that we will make that happen.

I’m sharing this because every conversation about files, approvals and transfers is about someone’s actual life. Three years of saving. A bill due. A plan that was finally about to happen.

You are entitled to be angry with Northvale. You are entitled to be angry with us too. I am not going to ask you to calm down or thank you for patience you may not have.

I’m sorry we put you in this position.

## Support and the next updates

Since Friday, we have received **1,900 support emails**. There are **three people answering them**, and the current reply time is around **two days**.

That is too long when you are worried about your savings. It is also the honest picture of where our queue stands. If your situation is urgent, please use **urgent@pinha.example**, with **URGENTE** in the subject, so we can identify those requests.

We will publish an update on this blog **every Monday and Thursday until this is resolved**. The next update will be **Thursday, 12 November**.

We will say what has changed, what is still blocked and what we can actually confirm. If there is no progress on a necessary step, we will say that too.

For today, the essentials are:

- **Withdrawals, deposits and round-ups remain stopped.**
- **Your money remains safeguarded, but we cannot move it until Northvale releases it.**
- **For urgent cases, email urgent@pinha.example with the subject URGENTE.** We are seeking individual releases; we cannot guarantee them.
- **November and December’s monthly fees are cancelled for everyone.**
- **Our next blog update is Thursday, 12 November.**

We know another post is not what you ultimately need. You need access to your money. Until that happens, we owe you clear answers, including when the answer is something we would rather not have to say.
